projects.title: Path Tracer & Gaussian Splatting
projects.summary: Custom Vulkan engine with **path tracing** capabilities. Simulates a **toroidal sensor** to perform geometric and photometric acquisition and generates a synthetic dataset for a **Gaussian Splatting** model.

blocks.text: **Path Tracing** alongside **Physically Based Rendering (PBR)** workflows is the standard technique for simulating physically accurate scenes. However, the computational budget required makes real-time execution challenging on commercial GPUs. This project places a virtual sensor inside a path-traced environment to scan it and generate a synthetic dataset for a **Gaussian Splatting** model, reconstructing scenes with Gaussian primitives for fast rasterization without sacrificing path-traced fidelity.

blocks.caption: Hardware-Accelerated Vulkan Path Tracer
blocks.text: The **Graphics Engine** uses Vulkan **Hardware-Accelerated Ray Tracing**. To eliminate Monte Carlo noise across perspectives, **Temporal Accumulation** blends frames over time, **Next Event Estimation (NEE)** accelerates direct lighting convergence, and a **Blue Noise texture** shifts residual error into high frequencies. Both **Metallic-Roughness** and **Specular-Glossiness** PBR workflows are supported.

Once the scene converges, a **Toroidal Sensor** performs dual acquisition: it samples the scene to generate a dense **Point Cloud** using several **Sampling** techniques (Halton, Uniform, Stratified, importance sampling methods, etc.), and captures multi-view photometric images along the centerline of the torus.

Decoupling geometric and photometric acquisition makes point cloud density independent of the number of camera views, enabling the Gaussian Splatting model to converge rapidly with a compact training set without sacrificing visual fidelity. Additionally, the convergence speed of the model shrinks as it does not need to perform heavy refinement steps such as the Adaptive Density Control (ADC), since the number of primitives is fixed by the acquisition phase. All the results of this project have been presented in the ECMS conference 2026.

projects.title: Nailed-It
projects.summary: 2D platformer developed in **Unity** combining precision platforming with custom point-and-shoot nail physics.

blocks.text: Developed for the Polytechnic University of Milan Game Design and Programming course, **Nailed-It** combines 2D precision platforming with projectile-based environment manipulation. As **Team Leader**, **Gameplay Programmer**, **Level Designer**, and **Audio Programmer**, I coordinated developers and artists from prototype to release.

blocks.caption: Custom Raycast Character Controller
blocks.text: Character movement and collision detection were **written from scratch** using Unity's **Raycast system** rather than built-in rigidbody physics. The controller implements variable jump heights, coyote time, and jump buffering inspired by Celeste and Hollow Knight.
The projectile system uses a dedicated secondary collider layer for nail attachment alongside mechanics for gliding, rapid respawning, and state-rewind.

projects.title: Real-Time Menger Sponge
projects.summary: Vulkan engine rendering recursive **Menger Sponge** fractals in real time via **Instance Rendering**, **SSBO Light Culling**, and an **Autonomous Camera**.

blocks.caption: Autonomous Pathfinding Camera
blocks.text: The **Menger Sponge** geometry scales exponentially with subdivision depth. Using Vulkan **Instance Rendering**, the engine renders millions of cubes while an **Autonomous Camera System** queries the spatial grid to interpolate collision-free trajectories through the fractal voids.

To support thousands of dynamic point lights without frame-rate degradation, the CPU pre-computes light influence radii and packs per-instance light indices into **Shader Storage Buffer Objects (SSBOs)** so each fragment evaluates only affecting lights.

projects.title: First Raster Engine
projects.summary: Custom **Vulkan Engine** built to explore explicit GPU memory management, the **rendering pipeline**, and 3D collision detection.

blocks.text: Built from scratch in C++ and **Vulkan**, this engine implements explicit command buffer recording, swapchain recreation, render passes, descriptor sets, and **Push Constants** for low-overhead CPU-to-GPU data transfers.

blocks.caption: Real-Time Gameplay & GJK Collisions
blocks.text: On top of the renderer, I built a time-trial racing game featuring a custom **GJK collision detection algorithm** restricted to lower mesh sub-volumes for efficient obstacle tests. Lighting is implemented exploiting **Phong** and **Cook-Torrance** shading models.

projects.title: OpenGL-SC vs OpenGL-Desktop
projects.summary: Comparative benchmark and determinism study of **OpenGL-SC** versus **OpenGL-Desktop** for **safety-critical** avionics and automotive systems.

blocks.text: Safety-critical systems in **avionics** and **automotive** domains require deterministic execution and static analyzability. This research benchmarks standard Desktop OpenGL against **OpenGL-SC** (Safety Critical) across instancing, compute workloads, and dynamic lighting.

blocks.caption: World of Cubes Benchmark
blocks.text: Comparing Desktop **Instance Rendering** against OpenGL-SC explicit draw calls demonstrated that while Desktop OpenGL achieves higher peak throughput, OpenGL-SC delivers tighter frame-time variance and predictable **Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET)**.

Because OpenGL-SC 2.0 omits native **Compute Shaders** and **Vertex Array Objects (VAOs)**, general-purpose fractal workloads were emulated via full-screen fragment passes and explicit per-frame vertex attribute binding.

projects.title: My Shelfie
projects.summary: Distributed client-server implementation of the **Cranio Creations** board game supporting **RMI**, **TCP Sockets**, **JavaFX GUI**, and **ANSI CLI**.

blocks.text:
Developed as the final project for my bachelor thesis, **My Shelfie** is a porting of a board game by Cranio Creations in Java.

Using a strict **Model-View-Controller (MVC)** architecture, **My Shelfie** hosts concurrent multi-player lobbies over a hybrid **Java RMI** and **TCP Socket** networking layer with automated heartbeat detection and disconnect state recovery.
